identity.title: CVE-Factory: Scaling Expert-Level Agentic Tasks for Code Security Vulnerability

problem.claim: Code-agent security capabilities require high-quality, executable vulnerability tasks for evaluation and improvement.

gap.claim: Existing approaches depend on costly, unscalable manual reproduction and use outdated data distributions.

contributions.claim: CVE-Factory is a multi-agent framework that automatically transforms sparse CVE metadata into executable agentic tasks.
The authors construct LiveCVEBench, a continuously updated benchmark with 190 tasks across 14 languages and 153 repositories, including emerging AI-tooling vulnerabilities.
The authors synthesize more than 1,000 executable training environments for code-security agentic tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe CVE-Factory as the first multi-agent framework achieving expert-level quality in this automatic task-transformation setting, and the training-environment scaling as the first large-scale scaling of agentic code-security tasks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Authors report 95% solution correctness and 96% environment fidelity when cross-validating against human expert reproductions.
Authors report 66.2% verified success on the latest realistic vulnerabilities.
Authors report that fine-tuned Qwen3-32B improved from 5.3% to 35.8% on LiveCVEBench, surpassed Claude 4.5 Sonnet, and improved from 12.5% to 31.3% on Terminal Bench.

narrative_sequence.summary: Security evaluation needs executable vulnerability tasks, while manual reproduction is costly and existing data can be outdated.
CVE-Factory automatically converts sparse CVE metadata into executable agentic tasks through a multi-agent framework.
The authors report high agreement with human reproductions and 66.2% verified success on recent realistic vulnerabilities.
The automation supports LiveCVEBench, over 1,000 training environments, and reported gains on two benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links an automated task-construction method to both a continuously updated benchmark and a large training-environment collection, then reports downstream model results.

lessons.interpretation: A contribution narrative is more informative when it connects infrastructure outputs to concrete evaluation and training consequences.
lessons.application: When introducing a data-generation pipeline, map each generated artifact to a named benchmark or training use and report the resulting metric change.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when downstream uses or outcome measurements are outside the work's scope.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluation protocols, sample sizes, confidence intervals, or definitions of solution correctness, environment fidelity, and verified success.
The basis and conditions of the Claude 4.5 Sonnet comparison are not given.
The abstract does not describe how continuously updated data are maintained or how the reported generalization was tested.
